struct_fields.comment: The fourth dword inside `sizeof`. The size is 0x1C, not the 0x18 of the three fields above, which is why every by-value string argument was four bytes short. **What these four bytes are is not established**: an allocator member of MSVC's _String_val would explain them, but BiceLib/GameClasses/CTrait.hpp read them live across its Hoi3CString[16] and found fragments of the parser's own buffer with nothing writing them, which fits trailing padding at least as well. Do not read it; it is recorded so the size is right.
struct_fields.evidence: Hoi3CString by value is 0x1C, not the 0x18 of its three recorded fields: `char[16]; int; int` has alignment 4 so MSVC inserts no padding between two of them, and four classes put a *named* non-string field at exactly string+0x1C with nothing in the gap - CMessageVariable (key 0x0, value 0x1C, previous 0x38, size 0x44), GuiTooltipText (0x0, 0x1C, 0x38, then int number at 0x54), CTechnologyCategory (0x8, 0x24, 0x40, then int index at 0x5C) and CBuilding (name 0x1C, displayName 0x38, then int index at 0x54). Decisively, BiceLib/GameClasses/CTrait.hpp records CTrait+0xE8 as a Hoi3CString[16] with a stride of 0x1C and checks it as 0xE8 + 16*0x1C == 0x2A8 - an ARRAY, whose elements are contiguous at sizeof intervals, so the stride IS sizeof regardless of what the fourth dword is. What would show this wrong: an array of Hoi3CString striding 0x18 anywhere, or a named field at string+0x18 in any class. What would show the *name* wrong: anything at all reading the dword.
